Backend: 7/7 pytest passed in test_router_update.py — POST temp router; PUT with new name/host/port/username/group/description and no password → 200, all fields reflected, no password/password_enc in response and GET /api/routers shows updates; PUT with password field also 200; PUT unknown id → 404; PUT name='a' → 422; PUT description length 201 → 422; PUT invalid port → 422. Real-router preservation test: PUT mr-65920574 with current values (blank password) + description 'QA edit check' returned probe.status='online' (proves stored password preserved through Fernet on blank), then restored description=''. Frontend E2E on public URL: pencil router-edit-mr-65920574 present, r-01 has no pencil; clicking pencil opens edit-router-modal (no workspace), prefilled name='IDC MONITORING', host='103.102.13.4', port='8728', username non-empty ('patrick'), password empty with placeholder 'Leave blank to keep current password', submit label 'Save changes'; cancel closes. Submit with description='QA desc' → toast 'IDC MONITORING updated · connection OK', fleet row shows QA desc under host, workspace subtitle contains QA desc, ws-edit-router opens modal prefilled with QA desc; clearing description and saving → subtitle no longer has 'QA desc'. Add router modal regression: title 'Add MikroTik router', submit 'Save router', password required, Description field present. Groups & Tenants Add group button still there. Real router host/port/username/password never changed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 231-241 update_router: after $set of update dict and re-probing, does a second $set only for probe fields — could be a single write. Minor; not a bug.

server.py RouterUpdate has no telegram_chat_id field (RouterCreate does). If a router had one at creation, it is preserved (only $set of provided fields), but there's no way to edit it via the UI. Consider adding to the model when Telegram-per-router routing is exposed.

AddRouterModal password field uses type='password' and placeholder text is visible only when empty — good; but `required={!editing}` means a browser 'required' validation won't fire in edit mode even if the user WANTS to change it (they can just leave blank). Working as designed but worth documenting.
App.js is now ~530 lines; still no split into feature components. Line 522 (fleet table row) is a 700+ char JSX single-liner — hard to review.

openEdit(r) doesn't validate r.id starts with 'mr-'; safe today since UI only renders pencil for mr- rows, but a stray call from elsewhere could open editor for a demo router (backend would 404 on submit).

The edit modal shares data-testid pattern with add-router-* fields; tests can only differentiate mode via container testid 'edit-router-modal' vs 'add-router-modal'. Fine, but the submit button testid is identical ('add-router-submit') in both modes.
